title: Define failover trigger signal hierarchy (priority, dampening, acceptance tests)
creator: Miles Thornton
links: Confluence: ADR-042 failover trigger signal hierarchy (sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy.json)
Slack: Trigger signal false positive discussion (sources/slack/eng-sre/1768464022-trigger-signal-false-positive-discussion.json)
body:
Background / problem
Today, region failover triggers are a mix of ad-hoc alerts and partially automated routing policies. We’ve had (a) false positives (staging + a couple prod near-misses), (b) slow detection for real regional impairment, and (c) inconsistent behavior between Hosted API and Dedicated routes.

This issue finalizes the trigger signal hierarchy, dampening/hold-down timers, and the acceptance tests that prove we can:
- detect real region impairment quickly,
- avoid failover on local/service-specific issues,
- avoid oscillation (flapping) under noisy signals,
- provide deterministic, auditable reasons for a decision.

Scope
- Define signal priority order + tie-breaks
- Define required corroboration rules (when a single signal is authoritative vs when we require 2+)
- Define dampening windows, hold-down timers, and minimum-stability criteria
- Define acceptance tests (unit + integration + staging drill) and sign-off checklist
- Align with dashboards/metrics labels to support on-call debugging

Non-goals
- Implement the region health service (ENG-2413)
- Implement burn alerts or metrics (ENG-2418)
- Rollback semantics (ADR-043 / ENG-2416) beyond what’s required to specify anti-flap constraints

Proposed signal hierarchy (final)
Priority is evaluated top-to-bottom. Higher priority signals can trigger failover even if lower-priority signals are “green,” subject to corroboration rules below.

1) Cross-region reachability (authoritative)
Definition: synthetic probes from at least 2 independent vantage points failing to establish TCP+TLS+HTTP/2 session to the region’s edge (or failing /healthz and a lightweight inference ping endpoint) within the probe timeout budget.
Trigger condition:
- Hard fail: >= 80% probe failure rate for 60s AND at least 2 distinct probe sources are failing (e.g., perf-canary + external vantage, or two independent PoPs).
- Soft fail: 40–80% probe failure rate for 120s requires corroboration from either 5xx burn OR elevated connect timeouts at gateway.
Why: reachability loss is the clearest “region cannot serve” indicator and is less subject to load-dependent distortions.

2) 5xx error burn (high-confidence)
Definition: SLO-style burn-rate computed on region-scoped request success for “served by region X” (not global DNS outcomes).
Trigger condition:
- Page-level: 14x burn over 5m OR 6x burn over 30m, with a minimum request volume floor (to avoid low-traffic skew): >= 200 req/min aggregated across Hosted API + Dedicated control-plane eligible endpoints.
Corroboration:
- For automatic regional failover, require either (a) reachability soft fail OR (b) tail latency burn (p99) OR (c) elevated gateway upstream reset/timeout ratio.
Notes:
- We explicitly exclude model-specific 5xx spikes (single model version) unless also seen in a region-aggregated “any model” view.

3) Tail latency burn (medium-confidence)
Definition: p99 end-to-end latency SLO burn (region-scoped) and p99 gateway upstream latency.
Trigger condition:
- 10x burn over 10m OR 4x burn over 30m, with volume floor >= 200 req/min.
Corroboration:
- Must be accompanied by either 5xx burn OR capacity headroom breach (see #4) OR reachability soft fail.
Notes:
- Tail latency alone can be caused by single tenant behaviors (large prompts, retries) and is therefore not authoritative.

4) Capacity exhaustion / headroom breach (gating + supporting)
Definition: fleet headroom signal: “available tokens/sec at SLO latency” and/or “queue wait time” crossing thresholds, plus autoscaling saturation indicators.
Use:
- Capacity is NOT a standalone trigger to fail over the entire region.
- Capacity can (a) corroborate latency/5xx signals, and (b) gate failover execution to avoid cascading overload in the target region.
Thresholds:
- Source region headroom < 5% sustained for 5m counts as corroboration.
- Target region must have >= 20% headroom for the impacted tier before executing automated failover, otherwise we enter degrade mode (load shed) instead of full flip.

5) Provider status / manual operator signal (manual override)
Definition: cloud provider incident confirmed OR explicit operator command.
Use:
- Manual override can bypass corroboration rules but MUST record an audit “manual_override=true” and the operator handle.

Dampening + anti-flap timers (final)
- Evaluation interval: 10s decision loop.
- Signal ingest freshness: reject a signal stream if last_updated > 30s; mark as “stale.” Stale signals cannot be used as positive evidence; they can only prevent “all clear.”
- Trigger dampening:
  - Reachability hard fail: 60s sustained before eligible.
  - Reachability soft fail: 120s sustained + corroboration.
  - 5xx burn: 2 consecutive evaluation windows (>= 20s apart) meeting burn threshold.
  - Latency burn: 3 consecutive evaluation windows meeting burn threshold.
- Hold-down after failover action (per route/tier): 20 minutes minimum before considering rollback or re-failover, unless reachability hard fail indicates the target region is now unreachable.
- Cooldown for repeated flips: max 1 automated flip per route/tier per 60 minutes (ties to ENG-2416/ENG-2426 hardening).

Corroboration matrix (quick reference)
- Reachability hard fail: no corroboration required (authoritative).
- Reachability soft fail: requires one of {5xx burn, latency burn, elevated gateway connect timeouts}.
- 5xx burn: requires one of {reachability soft fail, latency burn, elevated upstream resets/timeouts}.
- Latency burn: requires one of {5xx burn, capacity headroom breach, reachability soft fail}.
- Capacity headroom breach alone: never triggers; only supports/gates.

Do-not-failover scenarios (guardrails)
- Model-scoped impairment only (single model version) without region-wide error/latency symptoms.
- Control-plane only degradation where serving dataplane is healthy (e.g., inability to update routing policies). In this case, prefer degrade mode + manual routing change path.
- Target region fails capacity gate (headroom < 20% for impacted tier) AND we cannot shed load safely; prefer partial failover by tenant tier or keep traffic local with strong load shedding.

Acceptance criteria
1) Deterministic evaluation
- Given the same ordered signal set and timestamps, policy engine produces identical decision output.
- For every decision, we emit a reason code and evidence bundle reference (signal names + thresholds met + time sustained).

2) Unit tests (policy engine)
- Table-driven tests covering:
  - authoritative reachability hard fail
  - soft reachability + corroboration path
  - 5xx burn without corroboration does NOT trigger
  - latency burn without corroboration does NOT trigger
  - stale signal handling
  - volume floor behavior
  - tie-break ordering (reachability > 5xx > latency > capacity)

3) Integration tests (staging)
- Replay recorded signal streams via simulate endpoint (ENG-2428) for:
  - true positive: injected reachability loss in us-east triggers failover within <= 120s
  - false positive: transient 5xx spike from a single model does NOT trigger region failover
  - noisy probes: intermittent probe failures do NOT trigger without sustained threshold

4) Operational acceptance (on-call)
- Dashboards show the exact signals used, with an annotation for “eligible to trigger” and “trigger fired.”
- An on-call can answer within 5 minutes:
  - Why did it trigger?
  - Which signals were corroborating?
  - Were any signals stale/missing?

5) Success metrics (for game day readiness)
- Time-to-detect eligible impairment: <= 2 minutes for reachability hard fail scenario.
- No automated failover actions during 7 days of staging burn-in when injecting random single-service failures (synthetic).

Implementation notes / handoff
- This ticket is the spec + acceptance tests definition. Implementation lands across:
  - policy engine deterministic priority (PR-19812)
  - perf canary probes (ENG-2417)
  - SLO/burn metrics + alerts (ENG-2418)
  - region health aggregator (ENG-2413)

Open questions resolved
- Q: Should capacity be a standalone trigger? A: No; only corroboration + gating.
- Q: Is reachability always authoritative? A: Yes for hard fail; soft fail requires corroboration to avoid probe noise.
- Q: How to handle missing streams? A: Missing/stale signals cannot be used to trigger; they prevent “all clear” and should degrade confidence.

Definition of done
- ADR-042 updated with the final hierarchy + timers + corroboration matrix.
- Acceptance tests written down (this ticket) and referenced by ENG-2415/ENG-2416/ENG-2421.
- Observability alignment call with Allison/Sergio completed (labels + dashboard panels needed).
comments: 2025-12-18 (Miles Thornton): Creating as P0 since it blocks dry-run validation. We need a single source of truth for signal priority + dampening. Please keep Hosted API + Dedicated aligned; any deviation needs explicit rationale + per-tier config.

2025-12-20 (Ravi Menon): Drafted initial priority list based on brainstorm doc. Biggest debate: should capacity exhaustion be allowed to trigger? My leaning is ‘no’ due to risk of cascading overload; use it as gating/corroboration only.

2025-12-23 (Allison Grant): +1 to keeping capacity as a gating signal only. We can’t trust fleet metrics to be clean during partial control-plane incidents. Also want explicit stale-signal behavior; during the last rehearsal, missing probe stream would have flipped us to ‘unknown’ and we need deterministic outcomes.

2026-01-03 (Miles Thornton): Pulled in reachability as authoritative (hard fail) with corroboration for soft fail; aligns with architecture thread. Please ensure volume floors are specified for burn rates to avoid low-traffic false triggers on Dedicated small tenants.

2026-01-08 (Sergio Costa): For dashboards: we need a “decision trace” panel that shows (1) raw signals, (2) eligibility timers, (3) corroboration satisfied, (4) action recommended/executed. Also please keep failover_reason labels bounded (no free-form strings).

2026-01-10 (Ravi Menon): Updated spec with explicit dampening windows + hold-down timers. Added do-not-failover scenarios (model-scoped issues). Next: finalize acceptance tests and get sign-off from SRE + routing.

2026-01-14 (Rafael Mendes): On-call acceptance: the top question will be “is this regional or just one service?” Please ensure the matrix requires corroboration for 5xx/latency and that reachability probes have at least two independent sources.

2026-01-16 (Miles Thornton): Marking ready for review. This should be consistent with ADR-042. Any changes after this point should go through ADR update + explicit re-approval (to avoid moving targets before game day).

2026-01-20 (Ravi Menon): Shipped final hierarchy/timers to ADR-042 and added acceptance test checklist references. Closing as Done; follow-ups tracked in ENG-2415 (dry run outputs evidence bundle) and ENG-2418 (burn alerts).
